transcript.text: Bosch SMS2HVI67G showing E:25 and won't drain. A wine glass smashed in it last night if that's relevant?

I have noted the E:25 code on your Bosch dishwasher display. This is a controller report and does not prove a part has failed, so let’s check what remains after the programme finishes. Is there still dirty water sitting in the bottom of the tub (inside, under the lower rack)?
Yes, there's still water left in the bottom. It hums and buzzes when it tries to drain. Also, there's broken glass in there so I'm being careful, wearing gloves.

Thanks for letting us know about the water and humming sound. Please switch the machine off and unplug it first. Put towels down and have a shallow tray ready, as several litres of water may come out. Wear gloves because there can be broken glass in the sump. Take out the lower rack, then twist and lift out the filter from the bottom of the tub. Rinse it under the tap and clear any food, grease or glass from the sump underneath. The app shows a picture to help you locate these parts. Was the filter or sump blocked (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
Yes it was blocked - there were large glass pieces in the filter. I've taken them out with gloves on and rinsed it. I've also got the water out of the sump with a sponge.
Thanks for letting us know about that. Please run a normal programme again and see whether the problem comes back. Is it working normally now, or does the problem still happen?
I ran it and it drains now, no E:25 showing.

[Heading: Blocked filter / sump]
Thanks for letting us know that the dishwasher now drains correctly after you cleaned the filter and ran a drain cycle. It is very likely that the blocked filter was the cause of the issue, so no replacement parts are needed. To help prevent this from happening again, we recommend rinsing the filter every week or two.
